references.text: Moses warned Israel that disobedience would lead to scarcity and distress: "Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a willing heart when you had abundance of everything, you shall serve your enemies." The prodigal son experienced exactly this – after squandering everything, he began to suffer lack. See [ref:5 Mos 28:47-48|Deuteronomy 28:47-48].

Proverbs warns that drunkenness and gluttony lead to poverty: "For the drunkard and the glutton will become poor." The prodigal son's wastefulness illustrates this principle. See [ref:Ordsp 23:21|Proverbs 23:21].

"Whoever loves a merry life will become poor; whoever loves wine and oil will not be rich." The prodigal son loved a dissolute life and ended up in distress, just as this proverb describes. See [ref:Ordsp 21:17|Proverbs 21:17].

A warning that one's wealth may end up in the hands of strangers, leaving you sighing when your strength is spent. The prodigal son's situation, where he squandered his inheritance in a foreign land, reflects this warning. See [ref:Ordsp 5:10-11|Proverbs 5:10-11].

The prophet Amos speaks of famine sent by God – "lack of bread in all the cities." The famine that struck the country where the prodigal son was (λιμὸς ἰσχυρά) recalls biblical famines that show humanity's dependence on God. See [ref:Am 4:6|Amos 4:6].

In Acts, Agabus prophesies a great famine (λιμὸν μεγάλην) over the whole world. The same Greek word λιμός is used for the famine that struck the prodigal son, pointing to God's providence in times of severe distress. See [ref:Apg 11:28|Acts 11:28].

The previous verse tells us that the younger son "squandered his wealth with a dissolute life" – this is the direct cause of his lack in verse 14. Wastefulness meant he had nothing left when the famine came. See [ref:Luk 15:13|Luke 15:13].

The next verse shows the consequence of his lack: he had to take work feeding pigs and longed to eat the pigs' food. This reveals the depth of humiliation that began with the famine and the lack in verse 14. See [ref:Luk 15:15-16|Luke 15:15-16].

Abram went down to Egypt because there was a famine in the land. Famine as a driving force behind human actions is a recurring theme in the Bible, and the prodigal son's desperation was due precisely to such a famine. See [ref:1 Mos 12:10|Genesis 12:10].
